key_headlines.title: South Korea Revises Real Estate Tax System with Differentiated Criteria
key_headlines.summary: The government announced a real estate tax reform distinguishing between acquisition tax, property tax, and capital gains tax, with varying standards based on housing count, price, and actual residency to encourage owner occupancy.

key_headlines.title: Homeowners Returning to Residency Trigger Jeonse Shortage and Rent Surge
key_headlines.summary: Non-resident single-home owners are moving back due to higher holding taxes, causing a shortage of jeonse (charter) housing and forcing tenants to face rent increases, while landlords struggle with affordability.

key_headlines.title: Morgan Stanley Raises Korean Growth Forecast to 3.4% on Broader Economic Recovery
key_headlines.summary: Morgan Stanley upgraded South Korea's 2026 GDP growth projection by 0.6 percentage points to 3.4%, citing robust recovery spreading beyond semiconductors to non-semiconductor exports and domestic demand, while expecting faster rate hikes from the Bank of Korea.

key_headlines.title: SpaceX Reports 11 Trillion Won Q2 Revenue with 22 Trillion Won AI Infrastructure Investment
key_headlines.summary: SpaceX achieved 92% year-over-year revenue growth in Q2 2026 but recorded a net loss due to massive capital expenditure, with 158 billion dollars of AI-related investment reflecting intensified global competition in AI infrastructure development.

key_headlines.title: Single-Stock Leverage ETF Trading Volume Drops Below 1 Trillion Won on Regulatory Tightening
key_headlines.summary: Trading volume of single-stock leverage ETFs fell below 1 trillion won for the first time following regulatory strengthening measures including higher deposit requirements, indicating rapid decline in retail investor interest.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's real estate tax system has been fundamentally restructured with differentiated criteria for acquisition tax, property tax, and capital gains tax, creating significant market ripple effects. Non-resident single-home owners are returning to actual residency due to rising holding taxes, causing critical shortages in jeonse housing and driving up monthly rent prices across Seoul to unprecedented levels of 700 million won and 1.6 million won respectively. The government recognizes the severity of the housing supply crisis and plans to announce expanded housing supply measures for the Seoul metropolitan area shortly. This policy shift has triggered strong purchasing inquiry increases in mid-to-high price apartment neighborhoods like Mapo, Yongsan, and Gwangjin districts.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Morgan Stanley significantly upgraded South Korea's economic outlook, raising 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.4%, a 0.6 percentage point increase from previous estimates, citing broader-than-expected economic recovery beyond the semiconductor sector. The recovery is spreading to non-semiconductor exports and domestic consumption, prompting expectations that the Bank of Korea will accelerate its base rate hiking cycle, potentially reaching 3.5% annually by Q1 2027. Heat waves have emerged as a new economic concern, with extreme temperatures increasing by 44.9% since the 2000s and negatively impacting Q3 growth rates while driving up inflation through agricultural and energy cost pressures. India's central bank held its base rate at 5.25% while upgrading GDP growth forecasts, indicating cautious confidence in sustained demand despite manufacturing slowdown signals.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market rebounded strongly with KOSPI rising 3.8% on semiconductor sector strength, recovering above the 6,500 level with major chip stocks like Samsung Electronics gaining 2.5%, while KOSDAQ climbed to the 800 level for the first time in 13 trading days. Foreign institutional investors conducted 5 trillion won in net purchases, though domestic individuals and institutions maintained selling positions, suggesting cautious optimism about market recovery following last month's market bottom confirmation. The won-dollar exchange rate stabilized around 1,424.5 won as Middle East tensions eased, providing relief from recent volatility between 1,420-1,430 won levels. U.S. Treasury yields show pressure from AI-related capital expenditures, with warnings that massive infrastructure investments could push 30-year yields higher, potentially affecting global bond markets. Single-stock leverage ETF trading volume collapsed below 1 trillion won following regulatory tightening, indicating rapid retreat from leveraged retail trading positions.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's green industries face critical exclusions from the 'Korean IRA' tax support system, with electric vehicle and low-carbon steel sectors missing from production tax credit measures despite competitive pressure from China's surging EV sales and Japan's production-linked tax incentives. Critical resource security concerns are escalating as fluorite, essential for semiconductor and battery manufacturing, faces potential supply disruptions, threatening core industrial processes if export-import flows are blocked. Battery manufacturers achieved joint profitability in Q2 after overcoming the market 'chasm,' with multiple companies reporting turnarounds and positive policy expectations surrounding the Korean IRA implementation fueling analyst optimism about sector recovery potential. The climate ministry is preparing major debates on incorporating nuclear power into the 12th basic energy plan while balancing renewable energy expansion, signaling potential policy shifts in Korea's energy transition strategy.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's apartment rental market faces unprecedented pressure with average jeonse reaching 700 million won and monthly rent approaching 1.6 million won, driven by government tax policy changes encouraging actual residency and reduced private rental supply. Student district (school zone) apartments have emerged as top competitive demand drivers with over 100-to-1 application ratios, overshadowing traditional location advantages like transit-oriented development zones in the regional housing market. Property transactions have surged in mid-to-high price apartment districts (20-30 billion won range) in areas like Mapo, Yongsan, and Gwangjin following government announcement of ultra-luxury housing (over 3.2 billion won market value) tax targeting. City officials emphasize that fundamental solutions to market stabilization require sufficient housing supply through redevelopment and reconstruction projects rather than relying solely on tax measures.
sections.International Economy: The Trump administration is reviewing minimum 15% tariffs on imported polysilicon, the critical raw material for semiconductors and solar panels, potentially introducing additional minimum import price requirements that could significantly disrupt South Korean supply chains and renewable energy projects. The U.S. has refunded 100 billion dollars in invalidated Trump-era tariffs while continuing the tariff policy framework, with courts imposing repeated constraints on executive trade authority despite administration emphasis on tariffs as core economic policy tools. Trump called for U.S. interest rates to be 'the lowest in the world,' signaling pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve's decision, with CME futures markets pricing 58.4% probability of a 0.25 percentage point rate increase in mid-August despite Trump's dovish rhetoric. Currency volatility concerns intensify as strong won scenarios could deter foreign investment according to market analysts, while the Fed faces conflicting signals regarding rate adjustments amid inflation and growth dynamics.
sections.AI & Economy: SpaceX reported record Q2 revenue of 11 trillion won with 92% year-over-year growth but posted a 750 billion won net loss due to staggering 26 trillion won capital expenditure, with 22 trillion won dedicated to AI infrastructure including plans for space-based AI data centers beginning 2027 through enhanced NVIDIA partnerships. The Korean postal service and industrial bank are jointly establishing a 1 trillion won AI infrastructure fund targeting national data center expansion, signaling government commitment to supporting competitive AI infrastructure development. SK Telecom achieved strong Q2 results with 5.66 trillion won operating profit, a 67% increase year-over-year, driven primarily by AI data center business revenue doubling and demonstrating the sector's explosive commercial potential. Meta unveiled its first AI coding agent 'Muse Code' emphasizing price-competitive positioning strategy, while major tech companies continue massive AI investment commitments despite profitability pressures, fearing competitive disadvantage.
sections.Others: Single-stock leverage ETF trading volume collapsed from 12 trillion won to below 1 trillion won within one week following regulatory tightening measures including higher deposit requirements, marking the first time volumes fell below the 1 trillion won threshold and indicating rapid investor retreat from leveraged positions. Meta's introduction of AI coding agents and continued massive AI investment spending by major technology companies underscore the perception that falling behind in AI competition poses existential business risks, justifying continued expenditure despite profitability concerns. The U.S. State Department expressed optimism regarding potential negotiations with Iran and Oman on opening the Strait of Hormuz, suggesting diplomatic progress on Middle East stability issues that could influence global oil prices and economic conditions. Market experts debate whether regulatory measures on leveraged ETFs are effectively restraining speculative trading or merely causing tactical shifts in trading strategies among retail investors.
